prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a kitchen layout across five frames as the camera wearer turns left from a stove and upper range hood (0.6–0.8 m away, within arm's reach) toward a central hallway doorway (3–5 m deep) flanked by a counter/sink on the left and a refrigerator on the right (1.2–1.5 m away), before turning sharply right and tilting up toward overhead cabinets (0.4–0.6 m away) in frames 4–5. In frames 2 and 3, a bright silhouette on the left shows a man standing 0.6–1.0 m from the camera wearer—well within arm's reach of both the wearer and the counter behind him, and roughly 1.5 m left of the refrigerator—with his head and torso oriented toward the camera, while a very bright region on the far left of frames 4–5 lies 0.15–0.3 m away and partially occludes the cabinets behind it. Across frames 1 to 3, the microwave and stove recede and exit to the right as the camera rotates left and the man's silhouette grows slightly brighter and closer, before frames 4–5 shift to the close-up overhead cabinets and near-field arm/head edge cropped at the left border. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map more clearly separates the foreground man, mid-ground appliances, and recessed hallway planes into distinct distance layers and highlights the extreme proximity of the left-edge occlusion in frames 4–5. However, the depth map is unreliable for the distant person in the hallway (~4–5 m away, lost in uniform dark background), flattens small cookware on the stove in frame 1, and blacks out the ceiling and upper corners in frames 4–5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels discrete scene components across the camera wearer's turn: the refrigerator (1.2–1.8 m away) and elevated microwave (0.8–1.2 m away, above the counter and within arm's reach) in frames 1–2, the nearby man on the left (0.6–1.0 m away, within arm's reach and facing the camera wearer) in frames 2–3, a sink behind his left shoulder (~1.2–1.5 m away) and a second person standing ~4–5 m away through the central doorway (about 3.5–4 m behind the foreground man) in frame 3, and the close left-edge body region (0.15–0.3 m away) in frame 5. Relative positions and occlusions are reflected in the mask boundaries, where the microwave sits above and right of the refrigerator's rear edge in frames 1–2, the foreground man's lower body is cropped by the bottom frame edge while he partially occludes the sink in frame 3, and the refrigerator shifts to the right edge as the microwave rotates out of view. In frame 3, the map makes it much easier than the motion-blurred RGB to spot and isolate the distant person standing in the back room through the doorway. However, the segmentation map is unreliable across much of the scene: it completely misses the stove, range hood, countertops, and overhead wooden cabinets (even when within 0.5 m in frames 4–5), fails to detect the distant hallway person in frame 2 and the left-edge person region in frame 4, and hallucinates an unlabeled brown mask on the wooden cabinet door in the lower-right of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides sparse yellow keypoints on a black background, detecting only facial and upper-torso landmarks for the nearby man on the left (0.6–1.0 m away, within arm's reach) in frames 2 and 3, plus isolated spurious keypoints in frames 1 and 4, and no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In frames 2 and 3, the symmetric arrangement of the man's eye, ear, nose, and shoulder keypoints shows his head and chest facing directly toward and looking at the camera wearer at eye level on the left side of the scene, with his lower body unrepresented below the chest. Across the five frames, these facial and shoulder keypoints shift slightly downward and expand in spacing from frame 2 to frame 3 as the camera turns toward him and closes the distance from ~1.0 m to ~0.7 m, then disappear completely when the camera turns away toward the upper cabinets in frames 4 and 5. The pose map isolates the exact head orientation and gaze direction of the foreground man in frames 2–3 free from background clutter. However, it is highly unreliable overall: it misses the distant person standing ~4–5 m away in the hallway in frames 2–3, misses the close arm/head at the left edge of frames 4–5 (0.15–0.3 m away), fails to track the foreground man's arms and hands, and hallucinates a small skeleton cluster on the stove cookware in the lower-left of frame 1 (~0.7 m away) as well as a stray keypoint on the cabinet in frame 4.
